description: Governance crosswalk: framework controls mapped to the raucle evidence that satisfies them. evidence_field is a dotted path into the agent assurance packet (see docs/roadmap/overnight-sprint-backlog.md OV-1 shape); basis cites the repo artifact that backs it. UNSUPPORTED means nothing in the current raucle evidence plane satisfies the control: the validator surfaces this honestly rather than claiming coverage.

statuses.SUPPORTED: The cited packet evidence field carries real, verifiable evidence for the control.
statuses.PARTIAL: Some evidence exists but it is scoped or informal; the claim is narrower than the control.
statuses.UNSUPPORTED: No raucle evidence field satisfies the control. Honest gap, not a silent pass.

rows.title: Documented ICT risk-management framework
rows.basis: Trust model, event contract and bypass detection are documented as ADRs (docs/adr/0001-0005) and ops/runbook.md, which a firm can fold into its ICT risk framework; the packet itself only carries governance mapping slots, not the firm's legal framework.

rows.title: Logging of transactions and records for financial entities
rows.basis: Every gated tool call produces a sha256-pinned receipt (receipts.jsonl, ADR-0001/0002); the audit pack stages and re-verifies those bytes offline (ops/audit-pack/pack.py).

rows.title: Reporting major ICT-related incidents to authorities
rows.unsat_reason: The evidence plane detects and evidences incidents (SEC-001..SEC-011 findings) but no regulatory reporting pipeline or authority-submission artefact exists in the repo.

rows.title: Automatic logging of events over the lifetime of the AI system
rows.basis: Receipt chain over gated tool calls with tamper-evident hashes and independent verification; missing/invalid receipts are first-class findings (SEC-001, SEC-002), never silent.

rows.title: Robustness, accuracy and cybersecurity of high-risk AI systems
rows.basis: Red-run findings (policy fuzz, tamper, forge suites) and denial-rate/bypass rules measure attack resistance, but there is no formal accuracy standard or robustness certificate in the evidence plane.

rows.title: Human oversight measures for high-risk AI systems
rows.unsat_reason: No oversight-operator roles, approval workflows or human-in-the-loop evidence fields exist in the packet schema or repo.

rows.title: Documented AI-system impact assessment
rows.basis: The GOV-01 scoped assurance report (ops/assurance/generate_report.py, structural no-claim guard) and documented legal-compliance boundary provide assessment inputs, but no formal impact-assessment artefact is produced.

rows.control_id: A.9.7 AI system operation and monitoring
rows.title: Ongoing monitoring of AI system operation
rows.basis: Custody-coverage map (ops/assurance/config/coverage.yaml, ADR-0004) plus deterministic security rules (services/rules SEC-001..SEC-011) monitor every gated tool call continuously.

rows.title: Monitoring of system configuration and potential anomalies
rows.basis: Per-tool custody coverage defaults to unverified unless the gate signed receipts (fail-visible default), and registry changes surface as SEC-006.

rows.title: Detection of anomalous events and response
rows.basis: SEC-001/002 catch missing and invalid receipts, SEC-003/004 catch denial-rate anomalies and tool-side success after a correlated deny, SEC-005/006 catch looping and capability drift.

rows.title: Risk mitigation for the use of access credentials
rows.basis: Credential leases are observed on the custody plane for gate-covered tools (ADR-0004) with unverified tools reported fail-visible, but there is no vault-level credential custody control in the repo itself.

rows.title: Appropriate structures, policies and processes to direct and govern risk
rows.unsat_reason: Repository offers technical evidence only; no documented organisational governance structure or management-process artefact satisfies CAF principle B1.

rows.title: Systems that monitor security status and events
rows.basis: Receipt-chain verification with deterministic findings rules gives continuous, tamper-evident monitoring of the agent's tool surface, including what was NOT seen (unknown/missing states are first-class).

rows.title: Legal and regulatory requirements involving AI are documented
rows.basis: ADRs, the runbook and the compliance-honest reporting boundary document requirements handling; the packet carries mapping slots but no requirements register.

rows.title: The AI system is monitored for effectiveness of deployed controls
rows.basis: Red-run suites measure control efficacy directly: policy fuzz, gateway HTTP, mcp, tamper and forge attempts are receipted, counted and ingested as findings.

rows.title: Mechanisms for responding to identified AI-system issues
rows.unsat_reason: Findings are produced and evidenced but no remediation workflow, ticketing integration or response SLA exists in the repo; detection is honest, remediation is out of scope.

rows.title: Direct and indirect prompt injection
rows.basis: Gate policy proofs (staged and receipted by the audit pack, re-verified offline) plus the red-run policy-fuzz suite exercise injection resistance with receipted outcomes.

rows.title: Inadequate restriction of model/agent capabilities
rows.basis: The gate records the capability chain per tool call; privileged invocations without gate receipts fail visibly (SEC-001) and ADR-0001 pins the trust model for the boundary.

rows.title: Disclosure of sensitive or personal information
rows.unsat_reason: Findings never carry content (INDEX-PLANE only) and no DLP or disclosure-scanning control exists; the system cannot claim to detect sensitive-data leakage today.

rows.title: Agent granted excessive functionality, permissions or autonomy
rows.basis: Per-tool custody-coverage map bounds the agency surface; new privileged tools for an agent release fail visibly (SEC-006) and every privileged invocation is receipted.
